data.name: Dominga
data.gender_notes: Dominga is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Lady, Mistress, Mistress of the house
data.long_meaning: In Latin, 'Dominga' means 'belonging to the Lord'. Derived from 'Dominus' meaning 'Lord' and the suffix '-inga' meaning 'belonging to'. In Christian tradition, it represents dedication, devotion, and servitude to God. The name Dominga carries the meaning “Lady, Mistress, Mistress of the house” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Dominga usually hope their child will grow to embody lady, mistress, mistress of the house and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a strong bond and unwavering faith towards God.
data.etymology: Dominga belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lady, Mistress, Mistress of the house.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dominga total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Dominga' is deeply rooted in the Christian culture, representing a strong connection to faith and dedication to the Lord. Historically, it was popular among those who chose to name their children with religious reverence and in honor of their Catholic heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, 'Dominga' signifies surrender to the divine will, offering oneself completely to the Lord's guidance and protection. This name is considered to be a reminder of the importance of faith and humility, leading to a deeper connection to the sacred and inspiring a life filled with God's love.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dominga: Derived from the Latin word "Dominus," meaning "Lord" or "God," the name Dominga is a reminder of God's divine presence and sovereignty in our lives. It embodies the belief that every day is a gift from God, and each moment an opportunity to seek His guidance and grace.

historical_references.reference: Dominga of Aragon, daughter of King Peter III of Aragon and Queen Constance of Sicily, was born in 1317.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dominga remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Dominga from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Dominga - "Lady, Mistress, Mistress of the house". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
